questions.category: RAG 检索链路与向量库
questions.title: What distinguishes Advanced RAG from Naive RAG?
questions.source_text: What distinguishes Advanced RAG from Naive RAG?
questions.explanation: Advanced RAG improves all three stages: preretrieval adds query rewriting, query expansion and HyDE; retrieval adds hybrid search and better embeddings; postretrieval adds reranking, context compression and lost-in-the-middle mitigation. The key insight is that a raw user query is often a poor retrieval signal.

questions.category: RAG 检索链路与向量库
questions.title: What is HyDE and when is it useful?
questions.source_text: What is HyDE and when is it useful?
questions.explanation: HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings) prompts the LLM to generate a hypothetical answer, embeds that answer instead of the original query, and uses it for retrieval. It helps when a short or ambiguous query has a semantic gap from the documents; it is less suitable when generation cost or hallucinated terminology is a concern.

questions.category: RAG 检索链路与向量库
questions.title: How does hybrid search improve retrieval quality?
questions.source_text: How does hybrid search improve retrieval quality?
questions.explanation: Hybrid search combines dense semantic retrieval with sparse keyword retrieval such as BM25. Dense search handles paraphrases and conceptual similarity, while sparse search handles exact terms, identifiers and rare tokens; a fusion method such as reciprocal rank fusion combines their rankings.

questions.title: What is Agentic RAG and how does it differ from pipeline-based RAG?
questions.source_text: What is Agentic RAG and how does it differ from pipeline-based RAG?
questions.explanation: Pipeline RAG retrieves once in a fixed query-to-retrieve-to-generate sequence. Agentic RAG lets an LLM agent decide whether to retrieve, issue multiple queries, use tools beyond vector search such as web, SQL or APIs, and iterate until it has enough evidence.

questions.title: Explain the ReAct pattern and how it enables agentic retrieval.
questions.source_text: Explain the ReAct pattern and how it enables agentic retrieval.
questions.explanation: ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) interleaves reasoning traces with actions. An agent can reason that evidence is missing, call a search or retrieval tool, observe the result, and continue or stop. This enables multihop retrieval by following a chain of evidence that single-shot RAG cannot follow.

questions.category: RAG 检索链路与向量库
questions.title: What is Graph RAG and what problem does it solve that vector RAG cannot?
questions.source_text: What is Graph RAG and what problem does it solve that vector RAG cannot?
questions.explanation: Graph RAG replaces or augments a flat vector store with a knowledge graph of entities and relationships. It is useful for multihop relationship questions such as tracing a supply chain or finding common relationships between entities, which vector similarity alone does not represent explicitly.

questions.category: RAG 检索链路与向量库
questions.title: How is a knowledge graph constructed for Graph RAG?
questions.source_text: How is a knowledge graph constructed for Graph RAG?
questions.explanation: A typical pipeline extracts entities, extracts typed relationships, resolves duplicate mentions of the same entity, and stores the graph in a graph database such as Neo4j. Production systems also need entity quality checks and graph maintenance as documents change.

questions.title: What is Corrective RAG (CRAG) and what problem does it address?
questions.source_text: What is Corrective RAG (CRAG) and what problem does it address?
questions.explanation: CRAG inserts a retrieval evaluator between retrieval and generation. Each retrieved document is classified as correct, incorrect or ambiguous; incorrect results are discarded and ambiguous results are refined. It addresses the problem of blindly trusting a poor retriever or an out-of-distribution query.

questions.title: How does the corrective fallback mechanism work in CRAG?
questions.source_text: How does the corrective fallback mechanism work in CRAG?
questions.explanation: When local documents are scored incorrect or ambiguous, CRAG can issue a rewritten web-search query, decompose retrieved documents into relevant knowledge strips, and merge the refined local and web evidence before generation. The fallback prevents a weak local retrieval from being treated as sufficient evidence.

questions.category: RAG 检索链路与向量库
questions.title: What is Structured RAG and why is text-to-SQL retrieval fundamentally different from vector retrieval?
questions.source_text: What is Structured RAG and why is text-to-SQL retrieval fundamentally different from vector retrieval?
questions.explanation: Structured RAG retrieves from relational databases, spreadsheets and semi-structured sources by translating natural-language requests into executable SQL, rather than selecting semantically similar chunks. The result must satisfy schema, syntax, authorization and data-value correctness constraints.
